title: Throat exam (laryngoscopy)
what: An ENT doctor looks at your voice box and vocal cords, with a small mirror through the mouth or a thin flexible tube with a camera through the nose.
why: For hoarseness that lasts more than 2 to 3 weeks, a lump feeling in the throat, pain when swallowing, or a cough with no clear cause.
tell_doctor: Allergy to numbing medicines, especially local ones

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You are usually advised not to eat for 1 to 2 hours before. This makes gagging less likely. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: It is better not to smoke on the day of the exam.

prepare.title: Voice
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can write down when and how your voice changes. This helps the doctor.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit in a chair facing the doctor
Your throat or nose may be sprayed with a numbing spray
For an exam through the mouth, you stick out your tongue and the doctor holds it with a gauze pad
For an exam through the nose, the doctor gently puts a thin tube into your nose
You are asked to say "eee". This shows how your vocal cords move
feel: The spray tastes bitter and numbs your throat. It may feel like a lump
You may feel like gagging. Breathe slowly through your nose
The tube in your nose feels like pressure, but it usually does not hurt
after: After the spray, do not eat or drink until the numbness wears off, usually 30 to 60 minutes. Otherwise you may choke
The doctor usually tells you the result right away
If a small piece of tissue was taken for testing, that result comes later
red_flags: Trouble breathing or a badly swollen throat after the exam: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not. It can be unpleasant because of gagging, so a numbing spray is often used.

faq.q: When should I see an ENT doctor about hoarseness?
faq.a: If your voice has been hoarse for more than 2 to 3 weeks, see an ENT doctor.
